faq: Will exports handle large data sets?
Yes. Big exports are built in the background and offered as a download when ready, so the screen does not freeze. We test with a realistic number of rows.
Is it safe to share a report by link?
Links are random, read-only and can expire or be revoked. You can also add a password. We still advise sharing only what you are happy for the link holder to see.
Can the PDF match my brand?
Yes. We add your logo, colors and a title, and make sure tables break across pages sensibly. Send your brand files or a link to your site.
Does it work with my existing charts and tables?
Yes. We read the filters already on screen and export the same view. If your charts use an uncommon library, we tell you before starting if the PDF needs a different approach.
desc:
Export to CSV and PDF with shareable reports lets users take dashboard data into spreadsheets, emails and meetings. Ecom Swift LLC adds clean export buttons and private, expiring share links to your own app, so data leaves the screen the way people need it.

## Why do users need export and sharing?

Users need export and sharing because the dashboard is rarely the last stop for a number. A finance manager pastes it into a spreadsheet, a client wants a PDF for a board pack, and a colleague needs to see the same report without an account. If the product cannot do this, people take screenshots or copy cells by hand.

Screenshots lose detail and rows get missed. A built-in export keeps the data accurate and saves everyone time.

## How export features affect adoption and support

Export is often the feature that decides whether a dashboard becomes part of a team's routine. When people can take the exact filtered view into the tools they already use, they trust the product with more of their work. Reports travel further, and more people see the value of your app.

It also reduces support load. Without export, customers ask your team to run data pulls for them, which is slow for everyone. With a clear download button, they serve themselves. Shareable links add another benefit: a manager can send one private link to a stakeholder instead of forwarding a file that is out of date by the next day.

## What a great export and sharing feature includes

- A CSV download that contains exactly the rows and filters on screen.
- Clean column headings and readable dates, not internal field names.
- Large exports that run in the background, so the browser does not time out.
- PDF export with your logo, a report title and the charts included.
- Text encoding that opens correctly in Excel, including names with accents.
- File names that include the report name and date.
- Read-only share links that show a report without a login.
- Link expiry and a switch-off button, so access ends when it should.
- An optional password on shared links.
- A scheduled report sent by email on a set day.

## How we do it

We start with the screens where people most often ask for data. For each one, we agree which columns appear in the file, how dates and numbers are formatted and what the PDF should look like.

We then build the export so it uses the same filters as the screen. Large files are generated on the server and delivered when ready, rather than blocking the page. For sharing, we create unguessable links that open a read-only copy of the report, with expiry and a way for the owner to turn them off. The Basic package adds CSV on up to two screens. Standard adds branded PDF and more screens. Premium adds share links, expiry, a password option, a scheduled email and handover notes. We test with real-sized data so the downloads behave on your biggest accounts.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Export what the user filtered, not the whole table.
- Use plain column names that match the screen.
- Let share links expire and be switched off.
- Show progress when a large file is being prepared.
- Leave sensitive fields out of shared reports.

**Avoid:**
- Sending personal data through links that never expire.
- Exporting raw database field names.
- Making users wait on a frozen page for a large file.
- Sharing links that anyone can guess.
- Building a PDF that cuts charts across two pages.

## Who this is for

This service suits SaaS teams whose customers keep asking for spreadsheets. It suits agencies sending monthly reports to clients, and internal tools where managers need to share figures with people outside the app. It is also useful when a table already exists and only needs a reliable download button.

## What we need from you

Tell us which screens need export, who will use the files, and what the PDF should look like. Send your logo and a sample of a report you would be happy to receive.

We need developer or collaborator access to your code repository, and a test copy of the data. We never need your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until export and sharing are live.
